title: Deeper at matched FLOPs: DEPTH 8->10, dim 512->448
description: ASPECT_RATIO 64->44 and DEPTH 8->10 (n_layer 10, n_embd 448, 7 heads of 64), FLOPs/token 210.8M -> 209.2M; val_bpb 1.000256 at 411.3M tokens, MFU 28.78%, 48.7GB - a large loss on both throughput and quality-per-token.
reflection: Depth-10/dim-448 is a clear loss and the depth axis can be closed. Numbers: val_bpb 1.000256, 411.3M tokens, 1569 steps, MFU 28.78% (baseline 34.6%), peak VRAM 48.7GB, queued_s 331, FLOPs/token 2.0920e8 vs the baseline's 2.1077e8. I matched arithmetic to within 0.8% and still lost 15% of the token budget, because MFU fell 34.6% -> 28.8%: dim 448 is a multiple of 64 but not 128, so every GEMM is off the tensor-core tile, and 10 layers means 25% more Muon groups per step at the same tokens/step. Even token-corrected the run loses: extrapolating the //8 control pair (mean 0.989633 @482.4M) down to 411.3M at -0.000128/1M predicts ~0.9987, and I measured 1.00026, so roughly +0.0015 of quality-per-token penalty on top of the throughput loss - wide-shallow is the better shape at this scale, not just the faster one. The generalizable finding, and it is the second time this cell has produced it (see the window axis in #94/#95): FLOPs/token is not a currency for wall-clock here. Any future proposal budgeting a change by estimate_flops should be treated as unpriced until someone measures MFU at the new shape. Practical corollary for the remaining runs: keep n_embd a multiple of 128 and do not grow layer count - the per-step optimizer cost is already a visible slice of a ~190ms step.
